capabilities: Run coding agents in a built-in terminal emulator
Stream the active file path and text selection to Claude Code over a local WebSocket
Expose vault tools (getLatestSelection, getOpenEditors, getWorkspaceFolders) over a local MCP HTTP server
Show read-only diff previews of agent-proposed edits with terminal-gated approval
Switch between enabled agents from a dropdown and detect missing CLIs
disambiguation: Not just an MCP server; it also ships a full terminal emulator and a Claude Code IDE integration with diff previews.
extras: Manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff; the README discloses automated-review warnings for direct filesystem access and shell execution. Desktop only (no mobile); on Windows the built-in terminal does not work yet, though the MCP server and diff previews do. Free, no telemetry, no account; both local servers bind to 127.0.0.1 only.
motivation: The author wants LLMs to handle the brunt work in maintaining a knowledge base or task manager.
problem: Coding agents run outside Obsidian with no access to vault context, so LLMs helping maintain a knowledge base cannot see the active file, selection, or open editors.

relations.evidence: Connect Obsidian to coding agents like Claude Code and Codex so they can work with your vault context.
Exposes a modern Streamable HTTP endpoint at /mcp for Codex
This option runs ollama launch claude, which is Claude Code pointed at a local model
Full terminal emulator inside Obsidian, powered by xterm.js

requires.name: Agent CLI (claude, codex, or ollama + claude)
Python 3 on PATH (for the built-in terminal)
Anthropic or OpenAI account/key, depending on agent

summary: Runs coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Ollama) in a built-in Obsidian terminal and exposes the active selection and open editors to them over MCP.
